verdict.scope: the offline synthetic shadow coaching boundary at 3b14804 only
verdict.summary: CF-OBS-1 is enforced in both layers. The core reads the record's standing hold and keeps every review kind but the readiness declaration clinical whatever reference is sent (absent, stale, client-re-sealed, altered): 88 core cases and every app operation, no prescription over the hold. Custody composes the engine input from its stored copies, refuses every server-owned field and an explicit null reference, and suppresses any prescription while the record holds (defence in depth). The keyed chain and seal reject every edit, re-seal, reorder and truncation, and a foreign-key re-mac; ids are opaque and server-assigned; the clock is the server's; the closed payload refuses unknown fields without echo; reconciliation keeps the stored record (drop/change/duplicate refused, absent ledger = unchanged); idempotency, version conflict and the file lock hold; the whole-document-rollback residual is documented and PENDING an external monotonic version. No health word leaves custody across a full journey. Erasure cascades, the chain verifies with erased slots, the marker is read as a standing hold until a readiness declaration, and the account tombstone refuses resurrection: this is the SEC-V1CPI-06 tombstone design required in round 1. C8 now keeps a durable minimised trace, closing the prior C8 residual. Four new findings, all new, narrow and runtime-only, none a prescription leak or a hold bypass: SEC-V1CIB-01 (the adopt path does not re-check the standing hold after an erasure leaves a pending change) is the one integration-level defence-in-depth hole, bounded because the view still suppresses; SEC-V1CIB-02/03 (restart does not gate COACHING consent nor bind learningConsent) and SEC-V1CIB-04 (the erased slot keeps a keyless digest oracle) bound real collection, not this synthetic candidate.

findings.blocking: YES for INTEGRATION_READY (a defence-in-depth hole on the adopt path); NOT for the closure of this synthetic shadow candidate (no prescription leaks: planView re-derives from the record and suppresses).
findings.title: After an erasure leaves a pending confirmation, the adopt path installs it over the standing hold
findings.where: custody.eraseHealthFacts (does not clear doc.pending) and custody.accept/decline (do not re-check standingHolds).
findings.minimalReproduction: q1d G1 and q1b: a Situation-1 report (state REDUCED, not a hold) with a pending SCHEDULE_CHANGE, then eraseHealthFacts of the report. The ERASED_F08 marker now stands as a hold (view BLOCKED), but doc.pending survives, and accept swaps doc.program to the pre-hold proposal (programChanged=true). A normal review that forms a hold (submit) clears doc.pending; the erasure path does not.
findings.bound: planView computes blocked from standingHolds (the marker included), so the view stays BLOCKED with no prescription: no prescription leaves custody to the athlete. What leaks is a program-state mutation over a standing clinical hold.
findings.eligibility: new, narrow, runtime-only. Eligible for one narrow fix cycle and recheck. Fix: eraseHealthFacts clears doc.pending exactly as submit does when a hold forms, or accept/decline refuse while standingHolds is non-empty.

findings.title: The erased slot retains a keyless digest oracle of the erased health row
findings.where: custody.eraseHealthFacts keeps the chain entry's keyless digest (sha256 of canonical(row)) for an erased slot; the ERASED_F08 marker keeps the erased eventId in clear and the chain keeps recordedAt.
findings.minimalReproduction: q6 (a): chainDigest == keyless(row) before erasure; after erasure the digest is unchanged while rows[i]=null; the marker lists the eventId. For an operator with storage access, the digest is a brute-force oracle over bounded-entropy health content (condition x5, intent x4, ~20 sign booleans, days 3-14) with its identifiers known, so 'lose their content' is weaker than it appears. No inversion was performed; the fact is structural.
findings.bound: requires storage/operator access (the same actor the whole-document-rollback residual already flags) and real health data; the chain MAC (c.mac) is already keyed.
findings.eligibility: new, narrow, runtime-only. Fix: for an erased slot keep a keyed digest (HMAC) or verify from the chain mac alone, so the chain verifies without leaving the keyless oracle. Joint with G07 retention.
findings.owner: Engineering (fix), Security re-verifies; G07 for retention.

observations.note: declaredAt on an F08 fact is stored as the server's UTC instant (e.g. 13:00Z for a 10:00 -03:00 clock), not with the plan-offset suffix. This is the engine's canonical instant and is correct; it is the server clock, never a client-supplied time.

OBS-FFC-01: which clinical-guard paths return the actualLedger field changed between base and candidate (p9); custody treats an absent actualLedger as the record unchanged (q3) and falls back to the stored rows for the hold check, so the hold stands regardless. No data loss. Folded into C7.

The file store writes plaintext JSON (store.mjs notes 'access control at rest' as PENDING). Encryption and access control at rest, and erasure propagation to backups, belong in the Section 7 / G07 PENDING list.

The plan offset (timezoneOffsetMinutes) is athlete-provided at enroll and restart by design; an athlete can set their own plan's day boundaries. It does not bypass a hold (the hold comparison uses the same offset consistently). Acceptable; noted for completeness.

The clinical-carrier path no longer reaching G01's guard (the coverage gap QRE was asked to rule on) is QRE's; from security, every review kind still stays clinical over the record hold (q1 88 cases), so the gap creates no prescription leak.
